chapter_theme: Daksha's sacrifice (தக்கன் வேள்வி): a rite performed without Siva breaks down when he is angered, and the gods who took part are maimed for lack of his grace; yet Siva is the power within the very fire of the sacrifice, and after his anger he gave grace, so the devotee need not waver.
structure_note: The rite fails at Siva's anger (353, 354); Siva is shown as the nature of the sacrificial fire (355 to 357); the gods are maimed (358) and mantra used for gain is condemned (359); Siva's grace in destroying the asuras (360) and the closing assurance (361).

353.reading: When the Father, the Lord, grew angry, fire burst out through the blazing flame of Daksha's sacrifice, and the gods, unable to finish the worship they had begun, its order broken, scattered.
353.nuance: The verse does not tell the story's cause, Daksha's leaving Siva out of the rite; it assumes it. What it shows is a rite whose order (முறை) collapses the moment its true Lord is angered.

354.reading: Seeing the rite performed, Hari rose and said 'this one is not our lord; we have fallen into the binding snare of the world', did penance, and the endless one gave him grace.
354.nuance: Who says 'எந்தை இவன் அல்ல' and of whom is unclear: it may be Hari disowning Daksha, or a confession that they had taken the wrong lord. சந்தி may mean the twilight rite or simply the ritual. The penance-then-grace pattern is plain.

355.reading: Just so, in the sacrifice of Brahma's son the Prajapati, though the fire was a marvel, Siva entered into its very nature and stood exulting within it.
355.nuance: அப்பரிசே (in that way) opens every line, and the next verse repeats the device. அயனார்பதி is read as Daksha, a lord born of Brahma; ஆலிக்கின்றான் may mean exulting, roaring or dancing. The claim, as read, is that even a rite that excludes Siva burns only with his power.

356.reading: Just so he is the cause of Brahma, Vishnu and the other gods being what they are; just so, entering the fire on every day there is, he became that fire and stood blossomed forth.
356.nuance: The variants அலந்திருந்தானே (stood suffering, troubled) and அமர்ந்திருந்தானே (stayed seated) give different last words; அலர்ந்திருந்தானே (stood blossomed) is taken up by the next verse's opening, which supports it.

357.reading: While the gods praised him as the one who had blossomed forth, he looked hard at the low fire that confers lineage so that it was seized; the red Supreme went and caught it, and came running by the great way he delighted in.
357.nuance: குலந்தரும் கீழங்கி (the lower fire that gives lineage) and the last two lines are obscure; they may describe Siva, as Virabhadra, seizing the sacrificial fire. I can't fix the sense beyond that.

358.reading: Hari, Brahma, Daksha, the sun, the rising moon, the young goddess, Agni and Indra lost head, face, nose, hand and shoulder: without Hara's grace even those good ones were ruined.
358.nuance: The list follows the story in which each god at the sacrifice was maimed in one part, Daksha losing his head. The verse pairs gods and body parts only loosely. Its point is the last line: the gods are 'good' (நல்லோர்), and still fall without grace. வாலை is taken as a goddess, perhaps Sarasvati, whose nose was cut in the story.

359.reading: Gods who did penance and whisper mantras in the ear, who lay out the kitchen of the oblation with mantras and do ear-mantras looking to their own gain: such a gathered mantra is a cruel thing.
359.nuance: செவிமந்திரம் (ear-mantra, the whispered initiation formula) and குவிமந்திரம் (gathered or concentrated mantra) are technical. கொல் may be a doubt particle or mean 'kills'. As read, the target is ritual turned to self-interest, not mantra itself.

360.reading: When the many gods begged him to show grace, so that the nine fire-pits of the good might give joy, he who set blazing fire to the cities with his bow did so that the wicked asuras would perish.
360.nuance: நவகுண்டம் (the nine fire-pits) is a ritual term. The verse sets Siva's destroying the three cities beside the rite: his destruction here protects worship rather than breaking it, the reverse of Daksha's case. The tie between the two halves is my reading.

361.reading: Though even the clear-minded are shaken, do not you be shaken: the one we reach is our first Lord who sustains us, he of pure word who in anger destroyed Daksha's sacrifice and then gave grace.
361.nuance: The address turns to the listener (நீ). சுளிந்து ஆங்கு அருள்செய்த, angered and then giving grace, holds the chapter's two sides together. The tradition that Daksha was restored with a goat's head is not in the verse.

source_issues: 356: variants அலந்திருந்தானே and அமர்ந்திருந்தானே change the closing sense (troubled, seated) from அலர்ந்திருந்தானே (blossomed); 357's opening supports the text's reading. 357 has the variant அலந்திருந்.
358: variant சிந்தைகை for சிறந்தகை would add 'mind' to the list of maimed parts.
361: variant line 3 reads விளிந்தானத் தக்கனவ் வேள்வியை.
